subject: Private GPU pool sizing: runrate & warmup plan
messages:
From: Ryan Husain <ryan.husain@stratusai.com>
To: nikhil_sharma@redwood.com, laura_bennett@redwood.com
Cc: Emily Park <epark@stratusai.com>
Date: Tue, 13 Jul 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Initial sizing questions for our private GPU pool

Hi Nikhil / Laura,

Quick context: we (StratusAI) are kicking off a private deployment POC to run our recommendation and prompt-enrichment stack on a Redwood-managed private pool in our VPC. We want a recommendation from you on runrate sizing and a short warmup plan so we can scope procurement and rack/network.

Traffic profile (current POC estimate):
- Typical sustained: ~120 concurrent inference requests (avg response ~140 tokens)
- Baseline sustained QPS: 60 req/s (evenly spread)
- Peak bursts: ~750 req/s for 10-20 minute windows (launches / campaigns)
- Latency target: p95 <= 500 ms for the inferred responses (including any router hops)

Operational constraints:
- All traffic will go through our VPC peering; we need guidance on expected egress bandwidth per rack and per-GPU NIC sizing.
- KMS integration required (we will provide keys), and audit logs must be retained for 90 days.

Can you share a quick plan that covers:
1) a permissive starting pool size (nodes / GPUs) for the POC,
2) recommended warm pool / cache size and KV-prefix warming approach,
3) suggested autoscale thresholds and cooldowns to handle the 10-20 minute spikes, and
4) expected network egress per sustained and peak load so our infra team can size links

We'd like to replay 48 hours of production traffic once the pool is provisioned. Can you also confirm runbook steps for warmup and smoke tests?

Thanks — Ryan

--
Ryan Husain

Ryan — thanks for the profile. Below is a compact operational plan tailored for a single-rack POC, plus the artifacts we'll share (workbook + diagram). I'll mark assumptions so you can validate with your infra team.

Executive summary (POC start):
- Start footprint: 6 H100-eqs (single-rack). Expect multiplexed sustained handling of ~70–90 rps with batching + KV cache; repeated prefixes can yield 2–3x effective throughput.
- Burst strategy: reserve warm capacity for ~220 rps and autoscale in steps (2-GPU increments) up to an 18-GPU soft cap. Fallback routes to quantized model variants above cap.
- Network guidance: estimate 120–220 KB per response (depends on token count & metadata). Sustained 60 rps ≈ 10–13 Mbps; 750 rps peak ≈ 90–165 Mbps. Recommend 10 Gbps ToR for single-rack POC.

Detailed items you asked for:
1) Permissive starting pool
   - 6 GPUs: covers baseline and gives headroom for first replay + controlled bursts. Node layout depends on OEM; prefer 2–3 GPUs per host to reduce noisy-neighbor effects.

2) Warm pool & KV warming
   - Keep ~25% of GPUs in warm state for rapid response during short spikes (for 6 GPUs that is 1–2 GPUs).
   - KV prefix warming: pre-load top 15 prompt families (based on your replay frequency) before peak runs. Use a 3-stage ramp: 30m low-rate → 90m mid-rate → full replay. Track cache-hit ratio during each stage.

3) Autoscale & cooldowns
   - Trigger: sustained qps > 65 rps for 120s triggers scale-out.
   - Step size: add 2 GPUs per step; cooldown 180–300s to allow KV population and stabilize latencies.
   - Scale-in: only after sustained qps < 45 rps for 10 minutes to avoid oscillation.

4) Network / NIC sizing & egress math
   - Tokenization variance: lower-entropy responses ~120 KB; high-verbosity ~220 KB. Account for streaming overhead and TLS.
   - Sustained baseline (60 rps): 60 * 150 KB ≈ 9 MB/s (~72 Mbps) including overhead.
   - Peak (750 rps): 750 * 170 KB ≈ 124 MB/s (~992 Mbps). Plan for bursts of ~1 Gbps headroom in addition to internal control plane traffic.

Runbook (smoke & warm):
- Smoke 0 (sanity): node health, driver/firmware check, GPU mem, /proc/metrics (5–10m).
- Smoke 1 (small replay): 5% of replay for 10m, validate p50/p95 and token counts.
- Warm stage: run prefix-warming job against warm pool for 30–90m, monitor cache-hit and per-token compute time.
- Full replay: replay 48h window at scaled speed (start at 25% then ramp) while recording traces and model metrics.

Assumptions (please confirm):
- H100-equivalent perf profile; if you use older Ampere-class GPUs, throughput numbers will drop ~30–40%.
- Average response token size = 140; your actual distribution will affect egress and compute.

Artifacts: priv_pool_capacity_model.xlsx (detailed run-rate math), network_topology_diagram.png (ToR / peer / NIC recommendations).

Next step: I'll send the workbook and calendar invite for the review session. Laura / Vivek — please sanity-check NIC math and rack uplink guidance.

Best,
